🌍 Construire une équipe internationale composée de collaborateurs issus de 25 pays différents, avec une culture du télétravail très flexible

🤝 Gagner la confiance de milliers d'utilisateurs et obtenir d'excellents retours 

🚀 Déjà plus de 900,000 TPE/PME et plus de 6000 cabinets d’expertise-comptable utilisent Pennylane en France !

Pourquoi ce rôle est-il important chez Pennylane ? 

L’ANECS et le CJEC réunissent une génération qui contribue déjà à façonner le cabinet de demain : collaborateurs en cabinet, stagiaires experts-comptables, mémorialistes, jeunes diplômés, créateurs, repreneurs et jeunes experts-comptables installés.
Tous ne créeront pas leur cabinet. Beaucoup évolueront au sein de structures existantes et participeront directement à leur transformation : nouvelles pratiques de production, développement de nouvelles missions, adoption de l’IA, structuration commerciale, attractivité des équipes et amélioration de la productivité.
Pour les membres en phase d’installation, de reprise ou déjà installés, les enjeux sont très concrets : choisir les bons outils, développer leur activité, structurer les équipes et les missions, gagner en efficacité et identifier de nouveaux leviers de croissance. Pennylane a un rôle à jouer au-delà de celui d’un simple éditeur : devenir un partenaire de développement business et de productivité pour les cabinets qui se créent, se transforment et grandissent.

L’ANECS et le CJEC constituent un écosystème national et régional dense, avec près de 50 sections. Les bureaux se renouvellent en alternance, une année sur deux, ce qui demande une animation relationnelle continue et une transmission structurée entre les équipes sortantes et entrantes.

Ce poste est clé pour : 

- construire une préférence durable pour Pennylane auprès de la nouvelle génération de la profession comptable ;

- accompagner les membres dans leurs enjeux de carrière, de développement de cabinet et de transformation des pratiques ;

- transformer les partenariats, événements et prises de parole en contacts qualifiés, signaux d’intention et opportunités ;

- sécuriser une relation continue avec les instances nationales et les sections régionales ;

- faire de Pennylane un partenaire reconnu pour développer le business et la productivité des cabinets.

Comment vas-tu contribuer au projet ? 

- Tu construis et animes la relation entre Pennylane et l’écosystème ANECS-CJEC. Ta mission est de faire de Pennylane un partenaire de référence pour celles et ceux qui font évoluer la profession comptable : futurs experts-comptables, collaborateurs en cabinet, créateurs, repreneurs et jeunes installés.

- Tu combines une forte présence terrain, l’animation d’une communauté active, la construction de contenus utiles et un travail étroit avec l’équipe commerciale. Tu développes une connaissance fine des membres, de leurs parcours et de leurs besoins afin d’identifier les moments pertinents pour activer Pennylane : évolution professionnelle, projet d’installation, reprise, recrutement, développement de nouvelles missions ou besoin de gagner en productivité.

- Tu pilotes la relation nationale avec l’ANECS et le CJEC, animes le réseau des sections régionales et assures la continuité de la relation lors du renouvellement alterné des bureaux.

- Tu conçois et portes les activations les plus pertinentes : événements, ateliers, contenus, formats communautaires et prises de parole.

- En lien étroit avec l’équipe commerciale, tu contribues aux initiatives auprès des créateurs, repreneurs et jeunes cabinets. Tu développes une communauté qualifiée, identifies les signaux d’intention et assures la bonne transmission des opportunités aux équipes commerciales, au bon moment dans le parcours de chaque contact.

- Tu seras rattaché·e à Cyril Chanson, Manager Partenariats – Profession Comptable, et travailleras au quotidien avec les équipes Sales, Marketing, Enablement, Éducation et Événementiel.

Quelles seront tes missions au quotidien ? 
Pilotage du partenariat national — 20 %

- Porter la relation nationale avec l’ANECS et le CJEC de bout en bout : convention annuelle, gouvernance, budget, négociation des contreparties et plan d’activation.

- Gérer le budget sponsoring et événementiel, estimé à environ35 k€ par an, et en suivre le retour sur investissement.

- Sécuriser puis activer les contreparties les plus utiles : visibilité, contenus, prises de parole, accès aux sections, formats exclusifs et opportunités de qualification.

- Construire une relation de confiance avec les instances nationales et assurer la continuité du partenariat dans la durée.

Animation du réseau et présence terrain — 30 %

- Animer la communauté ANECS-CJEC au niveau national et régional, avec une présence régulière auprès des sections, de leurs bureaux et de leurs membres.

- Maintenir un mapping fiable des élus, ambassadeurs et relais locaux ; préparer activement les passations entre bureaux sortants et entrants.

- Construire et exécuter un plan de présence terrain ambitieux et priorisé : congrès, Estivales, DEC After, soirées jeunes inscrits, Olympiades, Journées des Jeunes Inscrits, tables rondes et événements locaux.

- Concevoir des activations utiles et engageantes : ateliers, témoignages, formats de networking, démonstrations, échanges entre pairs et prises de parole.

- Assurer le suivi post-événement : qualification des contacts, activation de la communauté, transmission des signaux pertinents aux équipes commerciales et partage des apprentissages terrain.

- Travailler avec la responsable événementielle sur la préparation et l’organisation des événements prioritaires.

Initiatives auprès des créateurs, repreneurs et jeunes cabinets — 20 %

- Co-construire avec l’équipe commerciale les initiatives destinées aux créateurs, repreneurs et jeunes cabinets : ciblage, calendrier, offres, contenus, événements et parcours d’activation.

- Apporter une connaissance fine des parcours, besoins et signaux d’intention observés au sein de la communauté ANECS-CJEC.

- Identifier les moments où Pennylane peut créer de la valeur : installation, reprise, structuration d’équipe, choix des outils, développement de nouvelles missions, vente, IA ou productivité.

- Qualifier et transmettre les contacts et projets à fort potentiel à l’équipe commerciale selon un processus partagé.

- Suivre, avec l’équipe commerciale, la contribution de ces initiatives au pipeline et au MRR attribuables au canal.

Stratégie d’activation, contenus et communauté — 20 %

- Définir et animer une stratégie de communauté combinant présence physique, rendez-vous digitaux, contenus, email, social media et relais locaux.

- Concevoir des formats utiles aux membres à chaque étape de leur parcours : réussite du diplôme, découverte des formes d’exercice, installation, reprise, développement ou modernisation d’un cabinet.

- Développer des contenus et événements autour des enjeux qui transforment les cabinets : IA, productivité, nouvelles missions, organisation, recrutement, développement commercial et expérience client.

- Formaliser les besoins, briefer l’équipe Enablement et coordonner la production des contenus.

- Construire, segmenter et animer dans la durée une base de communauté qualifiée, dans le respect des règles de consentement et de gestion des données.

Pilotage de la performance et veille — 10 %

- Suivre la couverture du réseau, les contacts générés, la qualité des leads, l’engagement de la communauté, les signaux détectés, le pipeline influencé, le MRR attribuable, le budget et le ROI.

- Produire un reporting trimestriel présentant les résultats, les apprentissages terrain et les arbitrages de priorisation recommandés.

- Assurer une veille sur les initiatives des concurrents auprès des jeunes professionnels de la profession comptable et proposer les réponses adaptées.

- Identifier les territoires, sections et formats les plus performants afin de concentrer les moyens sur les actions à plus fort potentiel.

Profil recherché : 
Tu disposes d’environ 4 à 6 ans d’expérience dans les partenariats B2B, l’animation de réseau, le community growth, le développement commercial indirect ou le marketing terrain à forte dimension business.
Tu as déjà évolué dans un environnement où il faut articuler une stratégie nationale avec des relais locaux : partenaires, antennes, ambassadeurs, clients et équipes internes. Tu sais transformer une présence terrain ou une communauté en dynamique mesurable de contacts, d’engagement et d’opportunités.
Tu apprécies particulièrement le terrain, les déplacements réguliers en région et les échanges directs avec des communautés professionnelles. Tu es autant à l’aise dans une relation avec un président de section que dans l’animation d’un atelier devant des membres, ou dans le suivi rigoureux d’une base de contacts et de ses signaux business.

Compétences indispensables :

- Animation de réseau et de communauté: créer des relations durables avec des interlocuteurs variés, identifier les bons relais, animer une communauté et maintenir la continuité malgré les changements de personnes.

- Appétence terrain: aimer aller au contact des professionnels dans les régions, participer à des événements et transformer une présence ponctuelle en relation durable.

- Partenariats stratégiques: piloter une convention nationale, négocier des contreparties, gérer un budget et faire vivre un partenariat au-delà de sa signature.

title: Responsable Déploiement / Implementation Manager
description:
Chez Lifen, nous pensons que les données médicales ont le potentiel de transformer le système de santé. Mais seulement si elles sont accessibles. Plus de données accessibles → moins de charge administrative, une meilleure coordination des soins et des découvertes scientifiques plus rapides.

Depuis 2015, notre mission est de libérer ce potentiel. Nos solutions basées sur l'IA permettent aux professionnels de santé de partager les informations médicales sans effort et aux chercheurs d'accélérer les découvertes cliniques : avec un impact sur des millions de patients en France chaque jour. Alors que nous nous préparons à nous développer en Europe, 2 choses déterminent notre succès : nos équipes et notre mission.

Aujourd'hui, plus de 150 personnes travaillent depuis nos bureaux et à distance pour libérer le potentiel des données de santé. Nous avons connecté 800 hôpitaux et 150 000 professionnels de santé, et nous ne faisons que commencer. Nous recherchons des personnes qui embrassent la complexité, veulent résoudre des problèmes difficiles et sont prêtes à construire le futur de la collaboration en santé.

🧩 Notre équipe Customer Operations

Chez Lifen, nous déployons nos solutions dans les hôpitaux de toute la France pour améliorer le quotidien des soignants et la qualité des soins.

L'équipe Customer Operations est le pont entre nos produits et les établissements de santé. Nous accompagnons chaque hôpital de A à Z dans l'implémentation de nos solutions : Lifen Documents & Lifen Intégration.

Notre équipe est composée de Project Managers et d'Operations Managers, tous pilotés par Loïc, notre Lead Customer Operations.

🎯 Ce que tu feras chez nous

En tant qu'Operations Manager, tu seras au cœur du déploiement de nos solutions dans les établissements de santé :

Cadrage projet : organiser et animer les réunions de cadrage avec les établissements pour comprendre leurs besoins techniques et fonctionnels, et définir la meilleure intégration de nos solutions dans leur quotidien ; adapter ton discours selon tes interlocuteurs (responsables IT, chefs de projet, utilisateurs terrain).

Accompagnement fonctionnel : comprendre l'organisation des services hospitaliers et les parcours patients pour adapter nos solutions aux réalités terrain ; challenger les besoins clients et proposer les meilleures pratiques.

Déploiement technique : configurer nos applications et flux d'interopérabilité (HL7), orchestrer les échanges avec les équipes IT des hôpitaux ; maîtriser les aspects réseau, serveurs Windows, déploiement applicatif et sécurité.

Recette & résolution : vérifier le bon fonctionnement de bout en bout avec les clients, diagnostiquer et résoudre les problèmes techniques ; qualifier les bugs et faire remonter les demandes d'évolution à l’équipe produit avec clarté et conviction.

Support expert : assurer le support niveau 2 en faisant le pont entre le support niveau 1 et la R&D ; monitorer proactivement les flux et certificats pour anticiper les incidents.

Amélioration continue : participer activement à l'optimisation de nos process internes et contribuer à des projets transverses ; partager tes retours terrain pour faire évoluer nos produits et nos méthodes.

Polyvalence produit : intervenir sur l'ensemble de nos solutions et développer une véritable expertise transverse.

⭐️ Ce que nous recherchons

Expérience en déploiement de projets à l'hôpital ou en healthtech avec déploiement hospitalier : Tu connais le monde hospitalier, son fonctionnement, ses contraintes.

Excellent communicant : Tu es à l'aise pour échanger avec différents interlocuteurs (IT, chefs de projet, utilisateurs), tu sais vulgariser et adapter ton discours.

Mindset doer : Tu n'as pas peur de mettre les mains dans le cambouis et d’être au coeur de l’opérationnel.

Autonome et proactif : Tu anticipes les problèmes, tu remontes rapidement les blocages, tu es force de proposition.

Compétences techniques (nice to have) : Connaissance en administration système (Windows Server, GPO), réseau (SFTP, VPN) et/ou interopérabilité HL7. Si tu viens de l'hôpital sans ces compétences, pas de problème, elles s'apprennent !

Passion pour la santé : Tu as un intérêt pour améliorer la qualité des soins et la vie des soignants.

💎 Nos avantages

- Une carte Swile avec 9€/jour (50% Lifen)

title: Field Marketing Specialist
description:
About Dust 

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it. 

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast. 

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50 .

This Role

The French market is one of Dust’s most important growth levers, and the Marketing team plays a central role in supporting pipeline generation through events, content and account-based activations.

As field marketing specialist, France, you will be the execution owner for Dust’s local Marketing activities. Working closely with the France Marketing Lead, you will turn defined priorities into high-quality events, localized webinars, social media, content and partner marketing activations that support Sales, BDRs and pipeline generation.

The France Marketing Lead owns the strategy, budget, programme selection and priorities. You will own execution, coordination, content delivery and continuous improvement across the French Marketing motion.

You will be part of a growing Marketing team across the US, UK and France, managed by the Global Head of Marketing.

Key Responsibilities

Own the execution of the French event and webinar programme

- Execute conferences, Dust-owned events and localized webinars selected and scoped by the France Marketing Lead.

- Coordinate the preparation, stakeholders, content, landing pages and logistics needed for a smooth delivery.

- Work closely with Sales and BDRs to prepare target accounts, follow-up plans and event-related content.

- Collect feedback, measure performance and document learnings after each activity.

Own French social media and content activation

- Own social media execution for Dust around events, campaigns and key French-market topics.

- Support AEs with relevant content and messaging for their LinkedIn activity.

- Coordinate with Global Marketing, Product, Customer Success, Design and external media partners to deliver relevant content for French enterprise audiences.

- Turn events, customer conversations and market insights into reusable content, including customer stories, blog posts, videos, YouTube content and Sales assets.

Support partner marketing and Growth programmes

- Provide execution and logistical support for regional partner marketing activities within the strategy, selection and budget defined by the France Marketing Lead.

- Support Growth with French-market content for ABM, webinars and paid campaigns.

- Produce or reformat assets such as e-books, landing pages, customer content and campaign materials.

- Connect event, content and partner marketing activities to target account engagement and pipeline generation.

Coordinate cross-functional Marketing initiatives

- Identify opportunities to automate repetitive Marketing tasks , Build Dust agents and workflows to support research, event preparation, content repurposing, Sales enablement, reporting and follow-up.

Requirements

- 3+ years of experience in B2B Marketing , ideally across Field Marketing, Event Marketing, Content Marketing or Product Marketing, preferably in SaaS or technology.

- End-to-end event ownership with the ability to plan and deliver conferences, executive events and Dust-owned events, from preparation through execution and post-event follow-up.

- Strong content and social media skills with experience creating or repurposing content for enterprise audiences across social media, landing pages, customer stories, YouTube, Sales enablement and executive LinkedIn profiles.

- Commercial and pipeline mindset with a clear understanding of how events, content and account-based activities support Sales, BDRs, direct pipeline and partner-led growth.

- Excellent communication skills in French and English , both written and spoken. You can write clearly and accurately, adapt your tone to different audiences and communicate credibly with enterprise executives.

- Generalist and hands-on approach . You are comfortable moving between event ownership, content creation, Sales preparation, webinars, campaign assets and operational coordination.

- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail . You anticipate needs, manage deadlines reliably and ensure that projects, events and content are properly prepared before launch.

- Self-starter mentality . You take initiative, make decisions, solve problems and own outcomes rather than waiting to be told what to do.

- Strong cross-functional collaboration skills . You know how to find and coordinate the right people across Marketing, Sales, BDRs, Customer Success, Partnerships and external partners.

- Nice to have: Experience marketing to French enterprise or CAC 40 audiences, working with agencies or media partners, supporting paid campaigns, producing webinars or video content, and working with tools such as HubSpot, Google Workspace and Figma.

- Location and travel: Based in Paris, comfortable working on-site and willing to travel occasionally for events in France.

What Makes This Role Unique

- Direct pipeline impact: Your work will directly support Sales and BDRs through events, content and ABM activations.

- Execution ownership in France: You will turn the priorities defined by the France Marketing Lead into high-quality events, content, social media and partner marketing activations in France.

- AI-native Marketing: You will use Dust to automate research, preparation, content production, reporting and follow-up.

- Generalist scope: The role combines events, content, social media, webinars, Sales enablement and ABM.

- Market-shaping opportunity: Help establish Dust as a leading voice in the French enterprise and agentic AI market.

Location 

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust 

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist. 

Learn how we think and work. 

- Our product constitution, a story about our mission 

- Agents at work - Latent Space , podcast with our cofounder, Stanislas Polu, 2024

- LLMs reasoning and agentic capabilities over time - dotAI, podcast with our cofounder, Stanislas Polu, 2024

title: Group Cost Controller
description:
About Us 

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role 

As Group Cost Controller at Harmattan AI, you will take ownership of the Group’s Industrial, R&D & other operational costing, working closely with the FP&A Manager to structure, develop, and continuously improve Industrial P&L, Cost performance monitoring, and decision-support capabilities across multiple entities.

The role combines hands-on analytical execution with higher-level structuring responsibilities, including Industrial P&L creation & development, Industrial & R&D cost planning, budgeting, forecasting, and KPI definition.

Responsibilities 

- Build the industrial P&L and the costing framework. Create the industrial P&L, define the standard cost calculation methodology, and set up the performance tracking processes that go with it.

- Monitor and challenge production and inventory performance. Track production costs, inventory levels and variances, identify deviations early, and work with operations to close them.

- Run the industrial management cycles. Initiate and own monthly closings, business reviews, forecasts and budgets for the industrial scope.

- Contribute to the Odoo implementation. Work with Production and Supply Chain to ensure inventory is tracked reliably in the system and that the outputs the business needs come out of it.

- Drive cost visibility and optimization beyond the plant. Follow R&D and project costs, and lead cost optimization initiatives across other operating costs.

Candidate Requirements 

- Educational Background: Finance, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field (Master’s preferred)

- Industrial Controlling Expertise: 5–8 years in cost or industrial controlling within a manufacturing environment or a complex production environment 

- Modelling & Tools: Expert-level Excel and strong financial modelling skills, plus hands-on experience with an ERP . Comfortable with BOMs, standard costs and variance analysis.

- Builder's Mindset & Adaptability: Has built a controlling framework from a blank page rather than inherited one. Autonomous, structured, and at ease in a fast-moving environment where the answer does not exist yet.

- Business Partnering & Communication: A true business partner — curious about operations, comfortable on the shop floor, able to challenge production, engineering and procurement constructively. Fluent in French and English.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

title: Product Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
Our Company "Buying Labs is the leading global partner for sourcing and distributing premium consumer goods!"

We're looking for a Product Engineer (m/f/d) to join our Tech team at Buying Labs ideally based in Hamburg or remotely for the right fit. In this role, you'll combine deep technical skill with strong product thinking to build tools and features using AI that create real value for our users and our business. You'll own features end to end - from scoping and design through development, deployment, and adoption - and use AI to build smarter and faster at every step.

This is a role for builders who care about impact: people who understand both the user perspective and the underlying business processes, who can scope what needs to be built and then make it happen.

Your Mission - End-to-End Product Delivery: Own features from concept to production and real users, not just code -ship complete solutions that drive measurable business value. Scope requirements, define technical approaches, and deliver across frontend and backend, with quality built in from the start and verified through appropriate testing.
- Product Thinking & User Focus: Understand user needs and business processes to identify what should be built and why. Translate product ideas and stakeholder input into shipped experiences that users actually adopt.
- Building AI into Products: Design and integrate AI-powered features into our platform - not just using coding assistants, but building AI solutions that solve real problems for our users. Identify opportunities where AI can speed up workflows, improve decision-making, or unlock new capabilities.
- Data Modelling & Scalable Systems: Build solid data models and scalable architectures that serve as a reliable foundation for our products. Turn repeated work into shared building blocks (UI components, data import flows, AI pipelines) so each new tool is faster to build than the last.
- Stakeholder Collaboration & Adoption: Work with stakeholders at all levels - from leadership to operations - to align on priorities and drive adoption of new tools and features. Communicate technical concepts clearly and build buy-in for your solutions across the organisation.
- Continuous Improvement: Gather feedback early, iterate quickly, and continuously improve what you build. Stay current with emerging technologies and engineering best practices to keep our tools & systems ahead of what the business needs to keep the platform competitive.
Nice to Have: 
- Experience with LLM tooling — provider APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini), agent and tool-use patterns (MCP), and evaluating output quality.
- Familiarity with vector search technologies (pgvector or similar).
- Hands-on experience with product analytics and observability tools (e.g. PostHog, Sentry) to measure usage and drive adoption.
- Experience integrating ERPs or operational systems (orders, inventory, master data).
- Background in eCommerce, wholesale, or B2B platform environments.
- Python for data tooling; Docker, GitHub Actions, AWS.

Your Profile - Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
- 5–8 years of professional experience in software development with a strong product mindset
- Strong experience with TypeScript and modern React. Backend experience with Node.js, Express or comparable, REST APIs, and PostgreSQL with practical SQL. For mostly building new applications on our modern stack (React 19, Vite, TypeScript, Bun) and occasionally working in an established JavaScript codebase. 
- Familiarity with modern AI/ML frameworks and agentic AI systems and solid skills in data modelling and building scalable system architectures.
- Comfort operating in a dynamic, fast-paced environment with shifting priorities.
- Hands-on experience building AI into products (structured extraction, automation, RAG, or agentic workflows), not just using AI coding assistants.
- Strong engineering quality mindset, with experience building reliable, maintainable products and validating them through appropriate testing.
- Strong product sense — you understand business processes and the user perspective, not just the code.
- Strong communication skills and experience working with stakeholders at all levels and driving adoption of the solutions you build.
- Proactive mindset with strong autonomy and initiative in a dynamic environment 
- Fluent English is required, German is a plus.

Why Us? - An awesome team & great vibes - Work with motivated colleagues in an agile, ambitious, and friendly atmosphere where collaboration and fun go hand in hand with high speed.

- Flat hierarchies & real growth opportunities - Take ownership of your role and develop personally alongside the company. We promote from within and value every voice, regardless of seniority or title.

- Modern workplace & cutting-edge equipment - State-of-the-art office setup including adjustable desks, mobile treadmills, air conditioning, and everything you need to excel in your role.

- Company pension program (bAV) - Smart pension plan with a 30% Buying Labs grant on your contribution—investing in your financial future together.

- Corporate Benefits membership - Access exclusive discounts from a wide range of partner brands and retailers.

- Full "Deutschlandticket" coverage - We cover the complete cost (ca. €60/month) so you can travel sustainably and conveniently throughout Germany.

- Free bike options - Choose between a complimentary "Swapfiets" bike (original or deluxe 7) or opt for JobRad bike-leasing with an additional €26/month grant from Buying Labs.

- Complimentary food & beverages - Free Friday lunch in the office, plus organic fruit & vegetables, drinks, snacks, coffee/tea, healthy shots and seasonal treats (e.g. ice cream, soups) throughout the week.

- Personalized workspace setup - €100 welcome voucher to customize and optimize your workspace from day one.

- Refer-A-Friend (employee referral program) - You love being part of Buying Labs? Fantastic! Then recommend people from your personal network and receive attractive rewards.

Sounds like a perfect fit? We can’t wait to meet you – apply now and be part of our journey!

title: Working Student Global Licensing (DACH) (all genders)
description:
Über tonies: tonies ist die weltweit führende interaktive Audio-Plattform für Kinder mit mehr als 10 Millionen verkauften Tonieboxen und 125 Millionen Tonies. Das intuitive und preisgekrönte Audiosystem hat die Art und Weise, wie kleine Kinder unabhängig spielen und lernen, durch seinen kindersicheren, kabellosen und bildschirmfreien Ansatz verändert. Tonieboxen wurden bereits in über 100 Ländern aktiviert, und das Portfolio umfasst rund 1.400 Tonies in mehreren Sprachen. Seit der Gründung hat tonies bedeutende Meilensteine erreicht, darunter die Börsennotierung an der Frankfurter Wertpapierbörse im November 2021 sowie ein global aufgestelltes Team von über 550 engagierten Experten, die aus verschiedenen Ländern agieren. 

Teil unseres tonies-Teams zu werden bedeutet, an einer inspirierenden Mission mitzuwirken: innovative und bedeutungsvolle Erlebnisse für Kinder auf der ganzen Welt zu schaffen. Gemeinsam gestalten wir die Zukunft des Spielens, Lernens und der Fantasie. 

Du als Teil von tonies: Bei Tonies Licensing haben wir es uns zur Aufgabe gemacht, die Magie von Audio zu Kindern überall auf der Welt zu bringen. Wir suchen eine motivierte und begeisterte Studentische Nachwuchskraft (m/w/d), die unser Portfolio an globalen Lizenzkonten unterstützt und dabei hilft, internationale Lizenzprojekte von der ersten Idee bis zum finalen Produktlaunch voranzutreiben. Diese Rolle ist perfekt für jemanden, der wertvolle Praxiserfahrung in einem kommerziell ausgerichteten Umfeld sammeln möchte – an der Seite eines Teams, das Beziehungen zu großen internationalen Lizenzgebern der Spielzeug- und Unterhaltungsbranche in Nordamerika und der EMEA-Region betreut. 

Deine Aufgaben umfassen: - Unterstützung im Lizenzmanagement: Du unterstützt das Lizenz-Team bei der Pflege und Koordination der Beziehungen zu internationalen Lizenzpartnern.
- Mitarbeit an internationalen Projekten: Du begleitest internationale Lizenzprojekte über verschiedene Phasen hinweg – von den ersten Gesprächen über den Vertragsabschluss bis hin zur Produktentwicklung und dem Marktstart.

What we are looking for: - Leadership & Team Empowerment: You have experience leading engineering teams—including specialists outside your own discipline—and excel at turning complex challenges into a clear vision. While your focus is on leadership and design, you can still dive into the codebase to unblock critical bottlenecks. 

- Architectural Vision: You advocate for modular, flexibly extendable, loosely coupled architectures with strong cohesion — so a feature can be built once and shipped across several hardware generations without being rewritten each time. 

- Strategic Product Alignment: You act as the bridge between engineering and product strategy. You translate business goals into technical reality and collaborate seamlessly across departments to keep our roadmap both ambitious and achievable.

title: Software Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
About The Company 

GROPYUS is a technology-based construction company focused on building multi-story residential buildings. Thanks to its prefabricated building system with various design options, industrial offsite construction, and fully digitalized processes, the company manufactures aspirational, sustainable, and affordable homes using timber construction methods. GROPYUS is using scalable construction and manufacturing solutions to tap into a future market, boost Europe's strength in innovation, while also playing a substantial role in improving sustainability.

About the Role 

You will be part of a highly collaborative product team working at the core of our manufacturing facility, transforming digital models into physical elements at scale.

Product Teams at GROPYUS own what they build, including underlying infrastructure, build pipelines, automated testing, release and rollout management, monitoring, and support. You will bring your experience in working with PLCs and/or other OT systems like e.g. robots, into the team.

As a Software Engineer (PLC / OT), you will work with your team on evolving the rather traditional architecture of MES like systems integrating via OPC-UA with PLCs into a future-proof architecture built with Software Defined Manufacturing in mind. You should be looking forward to developing less PLC / OT code over time and building a solution that allows for full simulation of upcoming manufacturing orders.

Furthermore, our teams are also responsible for operating and troubleshooting the software they have developed during working hours of the factory.

What you’ll be doing 

As a Software Engineer (f/m/d) on the Product Delivery team, you will be responsible for:

- Understanding and explaining the existing PLC / OT code base from our vendor to the rest of your team.

- Working together with your team and other teams in Product Delivery to evolve the current architecture into a truly Software Defined Manufacturing setup.

- Bringing an o perational mindset to monitor, maintain, and improve software uptime including reliable updates, latency, and efficiency

- Acting as a bridge between digital product delivery & physical logistics and manufacturing systems, ensuring both are aligned and integrated

- Helping define, monitor and evolve SLAs/SLOs as well as other important KPIs like e.g. OEE for critical systems

What you bring 

- You are an experienced software / automation engineer with experience in PLC or other OT technologies

- You are willing and excited to adopt modern software engineering approaches like code reviews, testing, CI/CD, etc.

- You have operated and supported large-scale software / OT systems

- You have worked in companies with strong operational cultures , ideally in logistics or manufacturing – understanding the commercial impact of system downtime

- You are proficient with most of the following technologies:

- PLC programming (TIA19 is a plus)

- Robot programming (KRL is a plus)

- OPC-UA

- MQTT is a plus

- Python / C++ / C# is a plus

- You are familiar with monitoring and alerting practices for production systems

- You have experience defining and working with SLAs/SLOs

- You are willing to travel to our manufacturing site in Richen whenever needed and within Germany and Austria for in-person team events

What We Offer 

- An unlimited contract with 30 vacation days. 

- Flexible, hybrid work: You can work from home or come into the office on the schedule that works best for you. Feel like traveling and working from another location? No problem. Tune into meetings and work from abroad for up to 40 days per year. In addition, flex hours allow you to prioritize important moments in your day. 

- Attractive perks and benefits : We offer a company pension scheme, language courses (English/German), and employee discounts with selected sustainable brands. Furthermore, our external partners in mental health support you in strengthening your mental health through anonymous private/group sessions. 

- Virtual Shares Program : Participate in the success of GROPYUS through our Virtual Share Program. 

- Ownership : You can truly make your mark with your work and contributions – on all our organizational levels. Find your solutions, drive and test them. 

- The chance to be part of something big : Our mission is to rethink an entire industry. Join us in reinventing construction and fostering sustainable, affordable living. 

- A diverse and enriching work environment : Become a valued member of a wonderfully diverse team of individuals from over 50 countries. At GROPYUS we value inclusion above all, ensuring that everyone feels they belong – no matter their background. In this way, our differences become strengths that help us grow as a team. 

Join us on our mission to design buildings as continuously evolving products to create the most exciting and affordable experience for all. We build for people and conserve the resources of our planet.

We can't wait to get to know you. 
For more information, visit our website .

title: Product Owner – Trust Services (eIDAS2, EUDI Wallet & Trust Platform) (f/m/d)
description:
IDnow is a leader in digital identity and fraud prevention in Europe with a mission to transform trust into the most powerful asset in the digital world, empowering enterprises with AI-driven, SaaS-based identity solutions that deliver scalable security, adaptive compliance, and real-time fraud prevention . Through its broad portfolio of digital identity and fraud prevention solutions, IDnow establishes, maintains and enriches trust throughout the customer journey, ensuring businesses can confidently and securely operate while leveraging digital identity to drive growth, security and scalability. 

The company has offices in Germany, United Kingdom, Romania and France , and is backed by renowned institutional investors, including Corsair Capital and Seventure Partners. Its portfolio of international clients spans a wide range of end markets including financial services, telecommunications, travel & mobility, gaming, and other industries. 

This position is based in Berlin/Munich, Germany or Rennes, France. 

IDnow is looking for Product Owner – Trust Services (f/m/d) to own the product direction, backlog and outcomes for a technical product area within IDnow’s Digital Identity and Trust Services portfolio. Working with a dedicated Scrum Team, this role turns customer, operational, regulatory and engineering input into a clear product goal, an ordered backlog and valuable, usable increments that can be released and operated safely. 

The most critical aspect of this role is serving as the accountable product interface between the Trust Services domain and Engineering: understanding the system boundaries, APIs, integrations, data flows and non-functional requirements well enough to make sound trade-offs, remove ambiguity and ensure that security, privacy, resilience, auditability and regulatory obligations are built into the product from the beginning. 

Key Responsibilities 

- Own the product goal, roadmap and backlog : prioritize by value, risk, dependencies and learning; keep decisions transparent. 

- Drive Scrum outcomes : lead refinement, support Planning and Reviews, clarify Sprint Goals, and use delivery metrics to improve flow. 

- Turn needs into buildable requirements : define user/system journeys, domain concepts, business rules, APIs, data states, errors, acceptance criteria and testable non-functional requirements – without over-prescribing implementation. 

- Partner on solution quality : work with Engineering, Architecture, Security, QA and Operations on service boundaries, technical debt, scalability, performance, availability, resilience, observability, incidents and operational readiness. 

- Own data, integration and lifecycle design : govern identity and audit-data flows, access, protection and retention; shape secure, interoperable APIs, including authentication, encryption, versioning, error handling and documentation. 

- Support releases and continuous improvement : define readiness, migrations, cutovers, deprecation, feature flags and rollback; participate in incident reviews and prioritize recurring quality, security and operational issues. 

- Translate regulation into product decisions : apply eIDAS2, EUDI Wallet, QES, QEAA/EAA, identity-proofing and trust-service requirements with Compliance, Legal, Risk and Trust Services SMEs, tracking adoption, reliability, quality, delivery flow and compliance readiness. 

- Collaborate across functions: align with Scrum Team s , Engineering leadership, Architecture, Security, SRE/Operations, Trust Services, Product, Compliance/Legal/Risk/Data Protection, Commercial and Customer Success, as well as relevant partners, relying parties and standards bodies. 

Preferred Experience 

- 4+ years of experience in Product Ownership, Technical Product Management, Business Analysis or similar roles in software and service delivery, including direct responsibility for backlog quality and product outcomes. 

- Hands-on experience working in Scrum or a comparable agile delivery model: ability to define a Product Goal, order a Product Backlog, write clear product backlog items, set acceptance criteria, participate in refinement and reviews, and make timely scope and priority decisions. 

- Strong technical fluency in modern software products and integrations, including REST APIs, JSON/Open API, authentication and authorization, OAuth2/OIDC concepts, webhooks or event streams, data models, service boundaries, API lifecycle and backward-compatible change. 

- Demonstrable experience working with regulated software and services, translating regulatory, security, privacy and audit requirements into actionable product requirements and delivery decisions, while balancing compliance, customer value, usability, scalability and time to market. 

- Practical understanding of secure software and service delivery: threat and risk thinking, software security, access control, encryption, secrets and key management, vulnerability handling, logging/monitoring, incident response, resilience and software supply-chain considerations. 

- Practical understanding of data lifecycle and privacy-by-design for identity and trust services, including data minimization, purpose limitation, sensitive evidence, retention and deletion, evidence, archival, data residency, audit trails and access transparency. 

- Ability to work with Engineering on system-level trade-offs without needing to be the implementing engineer, and to distinguish product decisions, architecture decisions, implementation choices, technical debt and operational risk. 

- Experience with service operations and lifecycle management, including release readiness, SLO or service-quality thinking, incident triage, post-incident learning, customer-impact assessment, migration, deprecation and support enablement. 

- Experience in regulated industries (e.g., financial services, telecom, public sector, payments, KYC/AML, digital identity, electronic signatures, PKI or trust services) is a strong plus, as is familiarity with eIDAS2, EUDI Wallets, ETSI standards or QTSP operating models. 

Perks & Benefits 

- Health & Wellbeing: Use your full access to the mental health platform nilo, including 1on1 sessions. 

- We value personal and professional development: make full use of Udemy, our training platform with 24/7 access and unlimited licences. 

- We make your remote work comfy: we provide support on equipment and offer flexible working hours. 

- We value collaboration & love to come together: regular onsite gatherings, internal initiatives and summer parties to connect across teams. 

- May your family require your attention or other reasons apply: use the benefits of our parental leave policy or our sabbatical programme. 

- In addition to the perks & benefits above, we offer specific benefits that differ between our locations.

description:

The Commercial Systems and Intelligence squad is a newly formed team within SumUp's Acquisition Mission under the Run & Grow tribe. We sit at the intersection of data, backend engineering, and sales operations, building the infrastructure that powers how SumUp attributes merchant acquisition, calculates commissions, and understands the full lifecycle of every merchant.

title: Senior Product Manager (JetBrains Context)
description:
Coding agents are only as good as the context they're given. Most explore a repository like a new hire on day one – grepping, opening files, guessing. JetBrains Context replaces that with actual knowledge of your whole codebase and resources, served to any agent that asks. If you want to own the layer that decides what an agent knows before it writes a single line, this is for you.

About JetBrains 

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

What you’ll do

This is a hands-on role where you'll manage the product from a terminal and agent session rather than slides. You'll bridge the technical core and cross-functional teams: collaborating closely with engineering and ML teams on indexing pipelines and retrieval quality, working with Air, IDE, and Junie teams on integrations, and partnering with marketing, developer advocacy, sales, and customer success on positioning and adoption. You'll take full ownership of defining problem statements, setting explicit trade-offs, and balancing cost, latency, and freshness across the platform.

Day to day, you will:

- Build and maintain a deep working understanding of chunking, embeddings, index freshness, retrieval, reranking, and agent-facing surfaces.

- Define and defend an opinionated vision for the product's evolution, including explicit target audiences, use cases, and key success metrics.

- Translate product strategy into actionable problem statements, priorities, plans, and milestones with an explicit definition of “done”.

- Communicate product direction clearly to engineering, leadership, cross-functional stakeholders, customers, and prospects.

- Analyze competing context and code-search products through direct use to establish clear differentiators and identify gaps.

- Define core operational and product metrics – index freshness, retrieval quality, agent task outcomes, adoption, retention, and unit economics – to guide decision-making.

- Represent the product externally by sharing roadmaps, publishing updates, speaking to developer audiences, and gathering community feedback.

- Partner with ML teams on model evaluation and platform teams on service scale, reliability, and cost.

What you’ll bring 

- A well-argued point of view on where AI-first development is going and what agents genuinely need from a context layer.

- Comfort with technical depth across embeddings, retrieval quality, sub-agents, tool-calling, indexing costs, and API design.

- The habit of using the product you build daily alongside competitors' tools.

- Communication that adapts to different audiences, from staff engineers and enterprise architects to conference attendees.

- A data-informed approach that combines telemetry, evaluation results, customer conversations, and market signals.

- Comfort with ambiguity and a preference for defining a new category over copying an existing one.

What you’ll need 

- Proven experience owning a complex developer, platform, or infrastructure product end to end, including strategy and roadmap.

- Hands-on familiarity with modern AI coding tools and agent workflows.

- The technical capability to work directly with engineering on retrieval behavior, APIs, data models, and integration surfaces.

- Experience communicating a product externally through written content, talks, or community engagement.

- Practical experience with search, retrieval, RAG, developer search, or static analysis at scale is a plus.

What success looks like 

Within your first months, you'll form and share a clear thesis for what JetBrains Context is and is not – one the engineering team recognizes as theirs and leadership can invest in. You'll establish a metrics story that distinguishes real retrieval quality from vanity usage, a roadmap with clear trade-offs, and a documented evaluation of serious competitors.

Longer term, success means JetBrains Context becomes a deliberate choice for developers and organizations, agents get measurably better answers because it exists, enterprises adopt it for its governance and scale, and the market clearly understands its unique value because you've communicated it effectively.

Let's shape the future of nutrition together and make Yazio the most successful nutrition app worldwide!

This role is 100% remote and open to candidates based in Germany, Spain, Portugal or the UK.

YOUR MISSION 

Our product generates billions of data points every month, and our development teams run hundreds of experiments a year. In your first year, you'll:

- Lead a small team of analysts embedded in our product squads. They're the ones measuring the impact of what engineering builds and helping figure out what comes next

- Be the analyst for Monetization yourself. You’ll handle tracking for new features, the experiments behind our conversion funnels and the reporting the squad runs on

- Set the example for how the work gets done. You'll write less production code than the analysts in your team, and the way you solve problems is what they'll pick up

- Set the data quality bar: what gets tested when data comes in, what gets tested once it's transformed, what gets tested in the reporting layer and what anomaly detection catches before a stakeholder spots it

- Move that responsibility upstream to the teams producing the data. Expect pushback from people who haven't had to think about it before

- Own the path from raw event data to curated, ready-to-use datasets in our self-service BI tool

- Take on the strategy side of squad analytics: how PMs and engineering managers use data when they make decisions

YOUR PROFILE 

You'll feel at home here if:

- You've been the analyst inside a mobile product squad. Event tracking, funnel and user journey analysis, experiments. You plan around release cycles and handle old app versions as a matter of course

- You've managed analysts without stepping away from the work yourself

- Experimentation is where you're strongest. You’ve run plenty of A/B tests, and you can talk through bandits, quasi-experiments and where Bayesian and frequentist approaches part ways

- You've built a data quality regime. You've held a number back because it didn't reconcile, then gone and fixed whatever let it through

- You write SQL all day and Python when you need it, and dbt is how you transform data

- When you take an analysis to a PM, it comes with what you'd do next. And when a number turns out to be wrong, you say so and change the process that produced it

Bonus points for:

- Experience with subscription businesses, including the mobile gateway SDKs (App Store, Google Play)

- Data catalogues like DataHub

- Warehouse: Snowflake

title: Head of Engineering (f/m/d)
description:
At Moss, we give finance professionals the power to automate their day-to-day and make forward-thinking decisions. 

Our culture is what makes that possible: we play to win, we obsess over quality, and we win as One Moss, and it works. Moss closed a €35 million Series C in August 2026, crossing a €1 billion valuation, and became one of Europe's fintech unicorns. Join us for what's next. 

We're hiring a Head of Engineering to lead engineering for one of our product tribes. You'll manage 15 to 20 engineers directly, with tech leads in each squad owning technical direction but no management layer between you and the team. You report to the CTO and sit in a tribe leadership trio with the Product Tribe Lead and Design Lead. Which tribe you'd lead is something we'll work out with you during the process.

This is a people leadership role with a hard technical requirement. The engineers report to you, so hiring, development, performance and pace are yours. At the same time you have to hold your own on system architecture: challenge estimates from your engineers, spar with the Product Tribe Lead on solutions, and know when a design is wrong before it ships. This role needs both.

How we're set up 

Tribes are the organisational body: people management, capacity, planning and reporting live there. Squads are assigned to problem spaces and run discovery and delivery, each led by a trio of Tech Lead, Product Manager and Product Designer. Tech Leads own the technical decisions in their squad, including estimates, and write code alongside their engineers. They don't manage people. You do.

We keep the structure deliberately flat. Management is anchored at tribe level, squad composition flexes to serve the most important work, and structure changes as we learn (roughly every six months in practice, not on a schedule). Discovery and delivery run in parallel: the next mission is scoped before engineers finish the current one, so engineers weigh in on architecture early and have the context to unblock themselves.

What you'll own 

- Feasibility and delivery for the tribe. You're accountable for tribe-wide delivery outcomes and velocity: the right problems, solved at the right quality, as fast as possible.

- The people. 15 to 20 direct reports. Hiring, onboarding, expectations, feedback, development, compensation and promotion recommendations, and the tough calls that keep talent density high. Tech Leads feed you performance signals; the decisions and the conversations are yours.

- Technical judgement across squads. Broad understanding of the tribe's systems and how they fit into the wider Moss architecture. You challenge estimates and technical proposals from your engineers; you don't produce the estimates yourself.

- A seat in the tribe trio. Roadmap and planning input through a feasibility lens. You argue solutions and trade-offs with the Product Tribe Lead as a technical peer, and push back on scope and timelines when the engineering picture says so.

- Operating rhythm. How the tribe plans, estimates, tracks and reports on delivery, with proactive, timely transparency to the tribe and to leadership, the good and the bad.

- Capacity. Putting your best people on the most impactful work, moving engineers between squads (and, where it serves Moss, between tribes) while still letting people build real domain depth.

- Alignment across tribes. Tribe leads aren't isolated trios. You align proactively with your peer Heads of Engineering and with platform and architecture owners, and you resolve shared-architecture questions through alignment, not around it.

How we expect leaders to operate 

- Velocity first, with high agency. Working smart and hard on the right problems.

- Lead by example, stay close to the work. You know the details of what your team is building and course-correct in real time. You get hands-on when speed or quality is on the line.

- End-to-end ownership of outcomes. Responsibility doesn't stop at your team's boundary. Make changes elsewhere when that's what it takes, communicating first, not unilaterally.

- No waterfall, no blame. Product, Design and Engineering work together from the start. If there's a gap in the trio, fill it or name it.

- Disagree and commit. Challenge when it matters. Once a call is made, own the message and explain the why, including for calls you argued against.

- Proactive expertise. We build expert products for finance teams. Decisions rest on real expertise, internal and external, not assumptions.

Moss has one manager framework for every people leader, and this role is held to it in full: build a high-performing team, define success clearly, deliver results with your team, and operate with speed and ownership. You can hold us to it too.

What you bring 

- 4 to 6+ years in engineering management , with a track record of managing engineers directly at a meaningful span. You've run hiring, performance management and difficult conversations yourself, not through a layer of managers.

- A senior engineering career before that. You've operated at senior or staff level as an engineer and your judgement on system design is current, not historical.

- Strong systems design. You can read an architecture, spot where it will break, and argue an alternative with the people who built it. You can tell a 2-week estimate from a 6-week one and explain why.

- Comfort as a technical peer to product leadership. You've shaped roadmaps and scope through feasibility arguments, and you've won and lost those arguments gracefully.

- Structure at scale without a middle layer. You build the practices that make 15 to 20 direct reports work: clear expectations, regular feedback, visible delivery.

- Fast in unfamiliar domains. You can reason about a new technical domain quickly and contribute before you have deep prior expertise in it.

- Experience from an environment with mature engineering practices : code review, testing, incident handling, planning and estimation that actually work. You know what good looks like and can build it where it's missing.

Strong pluses 

- Background at an AI product company or in ERP / financial systems. Both are directly relevant to what we build.

- Experience leading in a flat or tribe/squad-style organisation.

- Experience with a Tech Lead / Engineering Manager split, as either side of it.

What this role is, and isn't 

It's worth being clear about the shape of the job. Your technical contribution is judgement, challenge and architecture-level input; Tech Leads own the how and write the code alongside their squads, so this isn't a role with an IC workload attached. And it's a role where you manage engineers, not managers: every engineer in the tribe reports to you directly, there is no management layer beneath you, and we don't plan to add one. If that combination of deep people leadership and real technical engagement is what you're looking for, you'll find a lot to like here.

About Moss 

Moss is the Finance AI platform for Europe's mid-sized businesses, giving companies real-time visibility and full control over their spend. By automating card issuing, invoice management and expenses, Moss simplifies financial workflows and frees finance and accounting teams from manual, administrative work.

Founded in Berlin and used by more than 10,000 businesses including Flink, Schufa, n8n and Auto1, Moss has raised €220+ million to date and operates in Germany, the Netherlands, the UK and further EU markets. In August 2026, Moss closed a €35 million Series C led by Portage, crossing a €1 billion valuation and becoming one of Europe's newest fintech unicorns. Moss is backed by investors including Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Global Founders Capital, Cherry Ventures, A-Star.

We're a team of 300+ people from 50+ nationalities across 5 offices in Europe and we hire, reward, and grow people based on Moss DNA : playing to win, obsessing over quality, winning as One Moss. If that's how you want to work, we want to hear from you. - here's what else to expect: 

- Top-of-market compensation package, including equity. 

- Our vibrant offices are at the heart of our culture, where in-person time fuels collaboration and connection over weekly breakfasts and Friday demos.

- Additional benefits include: 20 days “work from abroad”, 600EUR/GBP Learning & Development Budget, and other local benefits.

Unless stated otherwise, benefits apply to full-time positions (interns and working students receive a tailored package).

title: Senior Product Design Engineer
description:
At Rohlik Group, we are building the future of e-grocery for over a million active customers across the Czech Republic, Germany, Austria, Hungary, and Romania. We own our entire technology stack — from storefronts and apps to automated fulfillment centers and last-mile logistics.

Within the Customer Experience (CUEX) domain, we own every touchpoint a customer interacts with, from the homepage to checkout and real-time order tracking across web, iOS, and Android. Our five storefronts run on a single product spine with localized content, pricing, and brand layers. We operate as a deliberately tight-knit, high-performing team where a Product Owner, Engineering Manager, Tech Lead, two Product Designers, and a dedicated full-stack engineering team ship fast, iterate constantly, and take full ownership of the end-to-end user journey.

Most interface failures in e-commerce aren’t layout issues — they are communication problems: what is said, in what order, and on which screen. As Senior Product Design Engineer, you will own the end-to-end design of all customer-facing surfaces across five markets. You will also manage our design system, Maia (our AI shopping assistant), and provide the design guidance that powers our automated coding workflows.

Why this role is exciting

- High-impact Group scope: Design every customer-facing touchpoint across web, iOS, and Android for five international markets, impacting millions of orders.

- True end-to-end ownership: Lead the complete lifecycle of product design — from initial problem definition and customer research to shipped A/B tests and real-world performance analysis.

- AI-first execution: Rohlik is an AI-first company. You’ll own the interface design for Maia, our AI shopping assistant, and build the structured design system guidance used by AI coding agents to generate on-brand code without hand-coding interfaces.

- Direct customer engagement: Lead user research and usability testing sessions directly with real shoppers, rather than commissioning external agencies or receiving filtered insights.

- High accountability, low overhead: Work in a small, autonomous team where design decisions move straight to production and work that doesn't deliver measured impact is honestly reverted.

What you will own and deliver

- Customer Surfaces: Own the end-to-end design and UX strategy across web, iOS, and Android for all core journey stages: homepage, search & browse, product pages, basket, slot selection, checkout, and order tracking.

- Design System as a Product: Own component architecture, design tokens, patterns, and documentation, ensuring our coding agents have precise design guidance to generate accurate interfaces.

- AI Experience Design: Define the interaction patterns for Maia (our AI shopping assistant), governing when it intervenes, how it presents information, and how it hands over to human support.

Head of AI Engineering

About Next Chapter Technology (NCT)

With a 15-year engineering history, a captive install base, and structured operational data, NCT sits at an inflection point to become an AI-first platform. As a Banyan Software operating company, we combine the agility of an independent business with the permanent backing of a global enterprise that buys, holds, and grows software companies for life.

The Opportunity

- Production AI Experience: Documented history of shipping functional AI/ML systems end-to-end to real users (data pipelines, modeling, deployment, and monitoring). You treat AI tooling as the core foundation of engineering productivity.

- The "Build-Solo" Appetite: Experience as a founding or first AI engineer who is completely comfortable delivering baseline architecture independently before relying on a large team.

- Measurable, predictable improvements in engineering delivery speed and cadence.

title: Engineering Manager - UK
description:
Hi I’m Colin , Director of Engineering, Europe. How do you feel about software engineers writing product specs, making product decisions, and not breaking down projects into individual tickets? If that sounds exciting (even if a bit scary), read on because I’m looking for an engineering manager to help us build a different type of engineering team and culture at Ashby .

To start, why do we need to be different? Time and again, I have witnessed engineers knowing what needs to be done yet being unable to get things done because of “the process” or because “more data is needed.” Some of the most effective projects have been skunkworks projects, where engineers have taken total ownership of a problem and driven it to completion. I want to normalize that at Ashby.

When we think about how these processes came about, we realize they carry a pessimistic mindset. They box people into smaller roles to minimize the chance of not meeting a certain standard. At Ashby. we’re building an environment that is optimistic about what engineers can own and achieve and embraces the innovative engineers (and frankly, often stays out of their way).

To accomplish this, our engineering leaders need to think deeply about individual performance, process, and culture - not running sprint planning or driving product and technical decisions. You’ll focus on building your team, their skills to thrive with the ownership they’re given, and an environment that empowers them to do their best work consistently, with little distraction. For junior EMs we try to stay within 6 direct reports. This enables them to spend time with our teams observing, correcting, praising, and, yes, coding. We like our managers to be hands-on while also making sure they’re not on the critical path.

We’ve already gathered an experienced, talented, and collaborative team of 25+ engineers. You’ll help me manage the growing team of engineers in Europe.

In addition to working with engineers you’ll also get to work on projects yourselves. Some examples of work our engineering leaders have done:

- 
Provide feedback on product and technical specs to help engineers identify where to cut scope or improve quality. You don’t make the final decisions, but you’ll influence and coach ICs to reach the right ones.

- 
Grow engineers to the point where they can take large, loosely defined projects, and deliver them with little intervention. They still ask for help when needed - the difference is that they’re driving.

- 
Jump into our systems and code to debug a customer issue, ship a small bug fix, or improve our developer experience. Engineering leaders at Ashby are great engineers and enjoy keeping their skills up-to-date (while staying off the critical path).

- 
Improve how we generate and simulate data in demo accounts. It’s a project off the critical path, but it helps you keep up-to-date on our codebase while immensely impacting the business, from Engineering to QA to Sales.

Why be a manager?

I had two experiences early in my career that set me on my path. I had a great manager who asked tonnes of questions about the decisions I was making and coached me without me realizing it. And I had a terrible manager - being told to work harder after a week of 3am finishes was not what I needed as a young engineer. The stark difference between these two experiences motivated me to become a manager: I wanted every engineer I worked with to have the support I had in the best case.

Since then, as I’ve learned more, I’ve realized that I love the kind of problems I get to solve as a manager. Deeply complex problems with long-term impact both on the company and on people’s lives. One of my proudest achievements is creating a fully transparent pay system, and on the day it was revealed, everybody was happy with it. Nobody stormed out. By spending time thinking deeply about everybody’s pay and ensuring the mechanics of promotion were clear, I put the team in a place where they could see a peer was paid more than them, and it not be a problem.

Despite all this, I love being technical. I sometimes indulge myself and spend a morning writing some code to improve tests or provide better abstractions. If I couldn’t be a manager, I’d be super happy to be an IC.

I’m looking for someone who is passionate. Passionate about both management and being technical. Someone who spots a pattern amongst their team, figures out a better way for us to operate, and then builds the automation that powers it. I introduced a new process that enables engineers to merge 30% of PRs without a human review beforehand. I also built the automation that approves these PRs. I also built that automation with abstractions that make it easy for the engineers to improve the automation themselves.

It can be hard to find seasoned engineering leaders who haven’t succumbed to the status quo in some way or another. We're committed to giving all our people a total and utter lack of terrible managers, and that means we're willing to take a chance on someone early in their leadership journey who's courageous, principled, and has the drive to build themselves into a great leader who can say “Yah I know everyone is doing that, but we won't because...”

Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply

Engineering leadership comes in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. I thought I’d outline some things I’m looking for to help you decide if this fits what you’re looking for:

- 
You love being technical and can hold in-depth conversations with direct reports from infra to backend to frontend.

- 
You enjoy management problems . We want people who get excited about driving people to be their best, giving difficult feedback, and building systems that make this easier

- 
You hold your team to a high standard and don’t shy away from getting into the details and giving feedback, even to the best folks on your team.

- 
You are an excellent and empathetic communicator. Facilitating change at both an individual and organization level requires understanding how to navigate the beliefs, opinions, and past experiences of engineers and figuring out how to both convince them of a new way of doing things while also leaving yourself open to feedback. 

- 
You know what exceptional engineers look like. You’ve thought deeply about what makes them tick, how to recruit them, and how to grow folks into them. I want to see depth here, the industry often regurgitates a vanilla description, but the reality is more nuanced.

- 
You’re good at thinking about product, business , and maybe even design, but you’re not interested in calling the shots and are more interested in building a team that can make the best decisions without you.

- 
You thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments . We're a young startup where leaders wear multiple hats, and you'll build your own (high-speed) on-ramp through developing strong feedback loops.

Put another way, you shouldn’t apply if: 

- 
You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology.

- 
You’ve gotten into management because it was the only growth path available

- 
You want to make all the product decisions instead of empowering your team to make those calls.

- 
You're happy with a team of engineers that are predominantly early-career, mid-career, or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. With enough guardrails, the team can get things done.

- 
A staff or principal engineer to you is someone who spends most of their time project managing or doing architecture reviews.

- 
You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently than the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent product delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers.

What We’re Building

Talent teams aspire to build a hiring process that identifies great candidates, moves them quickly through the interview process, and provides an excellent experience for the candidate. To accomplish this, recruiters perform thousands of daily tasks to coordinate and relay information between candidates, interviewers, and hiring managers. Teams struggle to keep up!

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example of our customers' challenges. A recruiter needs to collect availability from the candidate, identify potential interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and perform any last-minute adjustments as availability changes. They must perform this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 

Ashby provides talent teams with intelligent and powerful software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We put a lot of effort into designing products that are approachable to beginners but mastered and extended by power users. In many ways, spreadsheets set the bar here.

We have many customers, great revenue growth, years of runway, and amazing investors like YCombinator, Elad Gil, and Lachy Groom. I’ll share more once we meet.

Engineering Culture

Our engineering culture is motivated by Abhik and Benji ’s (our co-founders) belief that a small talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!).

Collaboration is Natural, Communication is Deliberate

Our engineering team (and the team at large) consists of lifelong learners who are humble and kind (meet them here !). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally (we filter for it in interviews). We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers can focus 36h out of a 40h work week (Abhik wrote about it here ). Even managers can rely on getting consistent time (and support to make, if necessary) to focus and do creative work without the demand of constant meetings.

Increase Leverage, not Team Size

We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:

- 
Great developer tooling. Our CI/CD takes ~10m, and we deploy at least 5x a day. Everyone on the team has contributed to developer experience 

- 
Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) which we are constantly improving. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video on it here ).

- 
AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here .

And a demo of one of these building blocks:

Give Engineers Ownership & Autonomy

We, as engineers, find clever ways to solve problems, which amplifies when we deeply understand the problem. All of us in technical leadership did our best work as engineers when we had a deep understanding of the end-user and the business and ownershi

I’ll share more details once we meet.



What We’re Building 


As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.


Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. TA software didn’t help.


As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!



Why You Shouldn’t Apply
